newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Scattered rains in Brazil soybean regions - Somar.
newsitem.headline: Scattered rains in Brazil soybean regions - Somar.

text.p: Rainfall will remain scattered in Brazil's key soybean growing regions leaving some areas with drier soil until the second half of the month, said independent meteorologists Somar.

"For the first fortnight in December, precipitation will be a little below normal in the southern regions," said weather forecaster Marcos Massari. "But this should return to normal in the second two weeks of the month."

A low pressure system was due to hit the Rio Grande do Sul region overnight on December 9, provoking isolated rains in the south until December 11. The front will then move south-east on December 12, Somar forecast.
"In the south, the conditions for rain will diminish and the sun will return to the whole region," it added.
A new cold front was expected to hit Rio Grande do Sul on December 15, again bringing with it cloud and rain.

Rainfall was very isolated in late November and early December, leaving some soybean growing regions with dry soil. But up to 112 mm of rain had fallen around Campo Mourao in Parana state on December 5.
